Subject: Request: vulnerability management evidence for SOC2 + SIG

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the intro — were starting our SOC 2 readiness review and SOC/Procurement asked for a bundled evidence packet showing Redwoods vulnerability management (VM) posture. Specific asks:

- Scan cadence: authenticated SAST/DAST schedule, infra/OS scanning frequency and responsible owners.
- SLA / remediation windows by severity (critical/high/medium/low) and whether Redwood issues credits for missed SLAs.
- Attestation that recent critical CVEs (we flagged CVE-2026-3451 and CVE-2026-4112) were triaged and remediated or mitigated in production.
- Any SIG/CAIQ/SOC2 artifacts you can share or a signed letter if needed.

Can you share a consolidated packet (artifact list + short attestation) and an expected delivery date? Procurement would also like to confirm whether DocuSign is required for the attestation.

Appreciate it — James
James Albright
Security Programs, NorthCoast Bank
security@northcoastbank.com
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: James Albright <james.albright@northcoastbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: vulnerability management evidence for SOC2 + SIG

James — thanks for the clear list. We can assemble a compact evidence packet and a short attestation letter for SOC2/SIG. Proposed plan:

1) What we'll include (packet):
   - Scan cadence summary (authenticated SAST: weekly; DAST: nightly unauthenticated plus weekly authenticated runs against staging; infra/OS vulnerability scans: weekly for critical assets, monthly full sweep).
   - SLA matrix (see below) and owner roster.
   - Recent CVE triage notes for CVE-2026-3451 and CVE-2026-4112, including mitigation path and closure dates.
   - Excerpted SIG/CAIQ references and pointer to our latest SOC2 Assertion Letter (redacted as needed).
   - Artifact index (logs, scan exports, JIRA references).

2) SLA / remediation windows (standard Redwood policy):
   - Critical (RCE/privilege escalation): target remediation or mitigated within 72 hours; emergency patch window and hotfix pipeline engaged.
   - High (local privilege / exploitable by authenticated user): target 7 days.
   - Medium: 30 days.
   - Low: scheduled triage in normal sprint cycle (60+ days).

3) Delivery: we can prepare the packet and attestation draft by 2026-11-22. If Procurement needs a signed DocuSign envelope, we can route the attestation through DocuSign and include the envelope link.

Ccd Kimberly (security) to confirm the CVE closure notes and add any required forensic artifacts. Let me know if you need the packet earlier or want a walkthrough call.

— Sofia Ivanova
Head of Solutions Security, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

James / Sofia — I pulled the CVE triage records and will include the following in the packet:

- CVE-2026-3451: flagged 2026-10-28, triaged 2026-10-29, mitigation deployed (config hardening + WAF rule) to production 2026-11-02, verification (post-deploy scan) 2026-11-03. JIRA SUP-9231 contains full triage timeline and remediation commits.
- CVE-2026-4112: identified as third-party dependency; remediation via dependency upgrade (v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0) completed in staging 2026-11-12; production rollout 2026-11-15 with rollback test; scan verification attached. JIRA SUP-9387.

I will attach: sast-scan-20261115.pdf (authenticated SAST export, redacted), vm-ownership-matrix.csv (owner by service), plus links to the JIRA tickets and scan run IDs. We will also include an internal attestation signed by our security lead confirming remediation dates; Ben can coordinate DocuSign.

Note on SLAs: we do not offer monetary credits for missed remediation SLAs today; escalation paths and engineering runbooks are the primary control. If Procurement requires credit language, that needs legal review.

Kimberly Park
